b_records.quote: Theorem 2. For η ∈ Θn(θ), we have R(X, n) ≥st R(Y, n). [Context:] Let X1, · · · , Xn be independent exponential random variables with respective hazard rates θ1, · · · , θn. The sample range of X = (X1, · · · , Xn) is R(X, n) = Xn:n − X1:n. En+ = {(x1, . . . , xn) ∈ Rn : 0 < x1 ≤ . . . ≤ xn}. For θ = (θ1, . . . , θn) ∈ En+, Θn(θ) = {η ∈ En+ : θ ≺ η and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2, . . . , n} and Ωn(θ) = {η ∈ En+ : θ ≺^w η and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2, . . . , n}.
